heading: Feature splitting also appears in larger models and open SAE releases
definition: the same pattern holds in large models and in open SAE releases, not only in a one-layer transformer.
summary: Beyond the one-layer setting the evidence is thin: one independent study finds finer versions of a single chosen feature in open Llama-3.1-8B SAEs, and two studies sharing authors with an original paper (Leask et al. 2025) find first-letter splitting in Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK SAEs but not in Matryoshka SAEs, which train nested dictionaries of several sizes at once. A second independent study finds that larger-SAE features nest only partly under smaller-SAE ones in Gemma 2 2B, and much less in Qwen3 4B; no study tests models larger than these.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B, thin. It rests on one independent supports verdict: arXiv:2410.20526, one selected feature at one Llama-3.1-8B layer, with all rows partial. arXiv:2602.11881, also independent, finds incomplete nesting in Gemma 2 2B and much weaker nesting in Qwen3 4B, with limits_scope verdicts only. The observed V2 rows come from arXiv:2503.17547 and lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN, which share authors with arXiv:2502.04878, a V1 original, so they are R1 evidence. They are first-letter results in Gemma-2-2B, either at a single size (arXiv:2503.17547's rows) or with no per-size trend (the lw post), and all of them are comparator rows. V2 would be R1 at 1-10B if the arXiv:2410.20526 example is not counted as an independent reproduction. No records at <1B, 10-100B or >100B (counts: V2.studies_by_size = {"1-10B": 2}). Toy / one-layer is V1's setting and is not linked to V2.

suggested_status.open_questions: Any linked study at >10B or on frontier-model SAE releases, using the size-growth measure, would set by_scale above 10B. A quantitative per-size sweep within an open release (several widths, several layers) would turn the partial rows into a clear yes or no. If such a sweep came from a group that shares no authors with an original (for example across Gemma Scope or Llama Scope widths), V2's R2 at 1-10B would no longer rest on one partial example. The per-architecture SAE Bench results in arXiv:2503.17547 (Figure 6, not in rows) would show whether splitting holds across architectures other than BatchTopK and Matryoshka. Is Qwen3 4B's weak nesting model-specific or a training artefact? Does Iris count arXiv:2410.20526's single selected feature at one layer, all rows partial, as an independent reproduction? If not, V2 is R1 at 1-10B. Which original should V2's author overlap be measured against? V2 has no original of its own (counts: V2.original_sources_linked = []), so this status uses V1's originals. The shared names found are with arXiv:2502.04878. If arXiv:2502.04878 is not counted as a V1 original, only Towards Monosemanticity is left, and the checked author file does not list its authors. The studies the reader linked to V2 but the verdict did not (counts: V2.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not = 8) are not named in the inputs. A V2 verdict on any of them, especially an open-release width series or a model above 10B, could change the level.

sources.headline: Llama Scope's Llama-3.1-8B SAEs had splitting-like finer features near a coarse one, in one tested layer.
A BatchTopK SAE on Gemma-2-2B spread a token's first-letter information over about three SAE features.
BatchTopK SAEs trained on Gemma-2-2B split broad features into finer ones.
Matryoshka SAEs on Gemma-2-2B did not show the splitting pattern.
Parent-child nesting in standard SAEs was partial on Gemma 2 2B, weaker still on Qwen3 4B.

wording_issues.issue: The tested models are Gemma-2-2B, Qwen3 4B and Llama-3.1-8B. counts: V2.studies_by_size has only the 1-10B bucket (value 2). No V2 record is above 10B.

Two releases are tested, each at one layer of one model. (1) Llama Scope at Llama-3.1-8B layer L15R (arXiv:2410.20526). The release is TopK SAEs (8x and 32x). The 8x Vanilla SAE in the same cosine comparison is a comparison SAE from outside the release. (2) The SAE Bench suite at Gemma-2-2B layer 12 (arXiv:2503.17547). Fig 6 compares the Matryoshka SAE with all six SAE Bench architectures (ReLU, TopK, BatchTopK, Gated, JumpReLU, P-Annealing) on absorption and splitting. These results are figure only. The text says Matryoshka reduces absorption and splitting compared with these baseline architectures. The only numbers in the text are for BatchTopK (65536 latents, L0 = 40): absorption 0.49, and first-letter information split across about three latents. The untested lines of arXiv:2602.11881 and lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN say they use their own trained SAEs.

'Families' could mean releases or architectures. Read as architectures, the pattern fails for Matryoshka SAEs. At Gemma-2-2B layer 12 (65536, L0 = 40), the Matryoshka comparator has absorption 0.05 and one latent per first letter, against 0.49 and about three latents for BatchTopK. The lw post's V2 verdict is limits_scope for the Matryoshka SAE at layer 8. The Llama Scope cosine result spans the Vanilla and TopK architectures.

The large-model evidence uses other measures than the version's size-growth replacement. These are: single-size absorption and first-letter latent counts (arXiv:2503.17547; its V1 verdict fix: not a growth progression); qualitative splitting with no per-size trend (lw r4); one feature compared at 8x vs 32x (arXiv:2410.20526); and parent-child co-activation that is incomplete (Gemma 2 2B baselines P(parent | child) 0.619–0.729; Qwen3 4B 0.309). counts: V2.rows_by_state = observed 3, partial 9. The observed rows (R7, R9, r4) all have role comparator.

method_sensitivity.what: Gemma-2-2B layer 12 (dictionary 65536, L0 = 40): absorption rate 0.05 (Matryoshka) vs 0.49 (BatchTopK). First-letter information is in one latent (Matryoshka) vs split across about three latents (BatchTopK). The study's method-sensitivity line says a weighted Matryoshka ablation does worse on absorption than equal weighting. Gemma-2-2B layer 8 (lw post, k-sparse probing on the first-letter task): first-letter features remain almost entirely unified in the Matryoshka SAE (r3), and they frequently split across several latents in BatchTopK SAEs at 2304–36864 latents (r4). The layer-8 contrast is qualitative, with no per-size values.

Gemma 2 2B layer 13, independent SAE baselines. P(parent | child) is 0.662, 0.634 and 0.619 at target L0 50, 80 and 100. P(child | parent) is 0.343, 0.326 and 0.317. Hamming distance is 36.1 at L0 50, 61.9 at L0 80 and 78.9 at L0 100 (Table 3). The verdict fix calls L0 100 the worst of the Gemma settings.

Gemma 2 2B independent SAE baselines at L0 about 50. P(parent | child) is 0.651 at layer 6, 0.662 at layer 13 and 0.729 at layer 20. The verdict fix calls layer 20 (0.729 / 0.395 / Hamming 30.6) the best nesting among the Gemma settings. The other V2 studies each test one layer (Llama Scope L15R, Matryoshka paper layer 12, lw post layer 8), so they cannot show layer effects.

status_amendment.public_note: We checked author overlap: two of the studies showing splitting in a larger model (Gemma-2-2B) share authors with an original paper, so they count as extensions by the original group, not as independent reproductions. The level stays R2 (independently reproduced), but it now rests on one independent example: a single feature in one layer of Llama-3.1-8B that shows the pattern only partly.
